prompt: A parking garage charges 4 dollars for any part of the first hour, 8 dollars for any part of the second hour, and 12 dollars for any part of the third hour. So the cost $C(t)$, in dollars, is $4$ for $0 < t \le 1$, $8$ for $1 < t \le 2$ and $12$ for $2 < t \le 3$. Find $\lim_{t \to 2^+} C(t)$.
hint: The $2^+$ means "a little MORE than 2 hours" — think $2.01$ hours, $2.001$ hours.

hints.text: The $2^+$ means "a little MORE than 2 hours" — think $2.01$ hours, $2.001$ hours.
A stay of $2.01$ hours falls in which price band? Check $2 < 2.01 \le 3$.
Any stay just over $2$ hours costs $12$ dollars, so $\lim_{t \to 2^+} C(t) = 12$.

explanation: Coming from the right means times slightly bigger than $2$, such as $2.01$ or $2.0001$.
Those all land in the band $2 < t \le 3$, where the cost is $12$.
So the right-hand limit is $12$. Notice $C(2) = 8$: staying exactly two hours is cheaper than staying one second longer.

alternativeExplanations.title: Stand on the step
steps: Draw the graph: flat steps at heights $4$, $8$ and $12$, each step a solid dot on its right end and an open circle on its left end.
Approaching $t = 2$ from the right, you are on the $12$ step. Approaching from the left, you are on the $8$ step.
Right-hand limit $12$, left-hand limit $8$, two-sided limit: none. Step functions jump.
